name: Antimony Yellow
lede: Antimony yellow is a light orange-yellow named for a pigment made from antimony, usually the same lead antimonate that painters knew as Naples yellow.

sections.title: Naples yellow or its cousin
sections.body:
The Pigment Compendium says antimony yellow, or yellow of antimony, was typically a synonym for lead antimony oxide, which is Naples yellow [1]. Nineteenth-century authors disagree: Osborn in 1845 and Salter in 1869 treat it as a different preparation of the same metal, deeper in color than Naples yellow, used mainly in enamel and porcelain painting [1]. A French manual of the time reportedly preferred it to Naples yellow as equally permanent [1].

Paterson says Naples yellow was used from the seventeenth century, possibly long before, in place of lead-tin oxide, and was later replaced by cadmium colors [2]. Paterson also says the name now refers to the hue, not the pigment [2].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: Our swatch comes from Ridgway's 1912 plate XV, and it is also in ISCC-NBS and Maerz and Paul, who date the name to 1839 [3]. It reads as a warm light orange-yellow, near [[apricot]] [3]. As ever with aged plates, the swatch is approximate [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color is moderately common in paintings, in 208 of 23,781, more than 67 per cent of named colors [4]. In 72 per cent of the 156 paintings where it is measurable it plays an accent role [4]. It peaks in the 1900s at 1.1 per cent of paintings, 1.4 times the museums' baseline [4]. The earliest match is Bernardo Daddi's work of 1333, centuries before the name, so that is a look-alike hue and not evidence of the pigment [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is a look-alike hue, not a pigment test. [4]

questions.q: What is antimony yellow usually a synonym for?
True or false: the old authors all agreed that antimony yellow equals Naples yellow.

openers: Antimony yellow is usually Naples yellow under another name, though some 19th-century writers called it deeper.
